task: Find all known gene-disease associations within PubMed.
task_instantiation:
Extract gene–disease association claims from PubMed paper text.

Definition (in scope): A gene (use the provided gene global_identifier) is explicitly stated to be associated with a human disease/phenotype/clinical trait, including:
- genetic association results (GWAS, candidate gene, case-control, meta-analysis) involving a named variant (rsID, SNP, allele, genotype, haplotype, polymorphism, mutation)
- statements that mutations/variants in a gene cause a hereditary disease (causal claims)
- disease-related differential gene expression findings (e.g., “reduced MDR1 mRNA in ulcerative colitis patients”) when the disease and gene are explicitly linked.

Out of scope (skip):
- purely mechanistic/biochemical function with no disease/phenotype link
- drug–gene interactions, pathway membership, or biomarker discussions that do not claim an association with disease risk/status
- associations stated only for a genomic locus/region without mapping to a specific gene (unless the passage explicitly assigns the signal to a named gene).

What counts as one record (granularity):
- Create ONE record per (gene × disease × variant/mutation/expression feature × genetic_model) when the passage provides model-specific statistics (e.g., dominant vs recessive ORs). Set `genetic_model` to the model name as written.
- If the passage reports the same gene–disease–variant association but lists multiple models/statistics without clearly separable single values, create ONE record with `genetic_model` null and put the full list of model-specific stats in `extra_details`.
- If no variant is mentioned (gene-level association, gene-based test, or causal gene statement), set `variant` to null.

Evidence threshold:
- Only extract associations explicitly stated in text (including stated values for OR/RR/HR/beta/p-value/CI). Do not infer direction or significance from context alone.
- Capture both positive and null findings (e.g., “not associated”, “P>0.05”).

Field instructions:
- `disease_name`: copy the disease/phenotype name as written.
- `association_label`: choose the closest label based on the author’s wording (risk-increasing/protective/associated/not associated/candidate/causal mutation/differential expression). If the text says “significant association” but no direction, use “associated”.
- `effect_measure` and `effect_value`: use when a single numeric effect is given (e.g., OR 1.15). If multiple effect values are given in the same record, leave `effect_value` null and put details in `extra_details`.
- `population`: capture ancestry/country/cohort descriptor if stated (e.g., “Finnish”, “Southeast Asian”, “north India”, “smokers”). Leave null if not stated.
- Put confidence intervals, multiple per-model values, Z-scores, tissue/cell type context for expression, and other nuances in `extra_details` when not captured elsewhere.

schema_spec.name: disease_name
schema_spec.description: Disease/phenotype/clinical trait associated with the gene, as stated in the passage.

schema_spec.name: variant
schema_spec.description: Specific variant/polymorphism/mutation/allele/genotype/haplotype implicated (e.g., rsID, amino-acid change, 'T allele', 'del/del genotype'). Null if the claim is gene-level with no variant named.

schema_spec.name: genetic_model
schema_spec.description: Genetic association model if specified (e.g., allelic, dominant, recessive, codominant, overdominant, homozygous, genotypic). Null if not specified or not applicable.

schema_spec.name: association_label
schema_spec.description: Direction/type of gene–disease relationship explicitly stated.

schema_spec.name: effect_measure
schema_spec.description: Type of quantitative effect measure reported for the association; use 'p_value_only' when only significance is given without an effect size.

schema_spec.name: effect_value
schema_spec.description: Single numeric value for the effect measure (e.g., OR=1.15). Null if not reported or if multiple values are reported in the same record.

schema_spec.name: p_value
schema_spec.description: P-value as stated (can include inequalities like '<0.01' or scientific notation). Null if not provided.

schema_spec.name: population
schema_spec.description: Population/ancestry/cohort descriptor tied to the association (e.g., 'European', 'Finnish', 'north India', 'smokers'). Null if not stated.

schema_spec.name: extra_details
schema_spec.description: Free-form string for additional details that do not fit other top-level fields.
